name: MuleSoft Anypoint
scope_notes: Covers MuleSoft Anypoint Platform. Anypoint Platform control plane (US/EU/Gov); IP allowlist only US/EU commercial; audit export needs Anypoint Integration Advanced or Titanium.

controls.name: Disable connected apps for the organization
controls.what: Org admin can turn off the connected apps feature for the whole org.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps (exact setting not named in docs)

controls.name: Authorization policy: Restricted (application allowlist)
controls.what: Only allowlisted apps can be authorized by org members; scope additions need re-approval.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > authorization policy

controls.name: Disable auto-approval of internal apps
controls.what: Under Restricted, internal apps must also be allowlisted.

controls.name: Revoke Authorization
controls.what: Removes an app's authorization and revokes its access and refresh tokens.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > Authorizations > ... > Remove

controls.name: Scopes per business group and environment
controls.what: App permissions are limited to chosen scopes, business groups and environments.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > Add Scopes

controls.name: Client secret expiration date
controls.what: Set an expiry on the connected app client secret.

controls.name: Modify the Client Secret for a Connected App
controls.what: Admin replaces the client secret manually or via Access Management API.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > app > Secret

controls.name: Delete Connected Application
controls.what: Deleting the app removes the client; effect on live tokens not documented.
controls.setting: Access Management > Connected Apps > Owned Apps

controls.name: IP Allowlist (Enforce IP restrictions for login)
controls.what: Blocks sign-ins with Anypoint credentials from outside allowed IPv4 CIDRs; users can be exempted.
controls.setting: Access Management > Security Settings > IP Allowlist
controls.plan: US and EU commercial clouds only

controls.name: Default session timeout
controls.what: Sets inactivity timeout that bounds bearer token validity (15-180 min).
controls.setting: Access Management > Business Groups > root org > Settings

controls.name: Revoke API contract
controls.what: Blocks a client application from calling the API instance.
controls.setting: API Manager > API instance > Contracts > Revoke

controls.name: Contract approval
controls.what: Instance owner approves access requests before credentials work against the API.

controls.name: Reset environment client_secret
controls.what: Change environment secret via KB procedure or support.

controls.name: IP Allowlist policy
controls.what: Gateway policy that only lets listed IPs or ranges call a managed API instance.
controls.setting: API Manager > API instance > Policies > IP Allowlist

controls.name: Revoke org connected app tokens
controls.what: Revokes all access and refresh tokens issued to a connected app.

no_control.what: IP allowlist does not apply to users who authenticate through SSO, so SAML-derived bearer tokens are not IP-restricted by it.

controls_unknown: Whether IP allowlist applies to connected app token requests or API calls with an issued token
Whether deleting a client-credentials app or rotating its secret invalidates unexpired access tokens
Whether a client-credentials app's tokens can be revoked without deleting it (Revoke Authorization is documented for user authorizations)
Exact UI setting name for disabling connected apps org-wide
Whether read/GET API calls are audit logged
Environment client secret rotation procedure (help.salesforce.com KB 001115221 did not render)
Whether IdP conditional access applies to connected app tokens (not stated)

credentials.name: Connected app that acts on its own behalf (client credentials)

authentication.summary: App posts client_id and client_secret to /accounts/api/v2/oauth2/token and gets a 60-minute bearer token; no user, SSO or MFA step is involved (MuleSoft points CI/CD to connected apps when enabling MFA; connected apps are exempt from reauthentication). Query results use the scope of the user who created the app.

federation.details: No inbound workload federation documented. The openid:google_wif scope is outbound: Anypoint acts as IdP for Google Cloud WIF.

ip_restriction.boundary: The org IP allowlist covers only user sign-ins with Anypoint credentials; client-credentials token requests are not user sign-ins. No per-app IP restriction documented.

lifetime.summary: 60-min access token; client secret no expiry by default, expiry settable

renewal.summary: Re-run client_credentials grant with the secret.

administration.summary: Org admins in the root org or business group create, edit, rotate secret, and delete. Scopes map to platform permissions and can be limited per business group and environment.
administration.conditions: Organization Administrator permission; up to 2000 apps per org.

offboard.details: When the creating user is deleted or removed, the app's ownership moves to the root org owner and the app keeps working; docs tell admins to rotate secrets manually.

inventory.details: Access Management > Connected Apps (Owned Apps) and GET /accounts/api/organizations/{organizationId}/connectedApplications.

log_sources.name: Anypoint Platform audit log (Access Management > Audit Log, Audit Log Query API)
log_sources.notes: Default retention 1 year (6 years for orgs before 2023-07-10), configurable 30-2190 days; export via Telemetry Exporter needs Anypoint Integration Advanced or Titanium.

containment.steps: Rotate the secret (Modify the Client Secret) or delete the app in Access Management > Connected Apps; remove scopes.
containment.notes: DELETE /accounts/api/organizations/{organizationId}/connectedApplications/{clientId}/revoke revokes all access and refresh tokens issued to the app. Rotating the secret alone is not documented to kill issued tokens.

credentials.name: Connected app that acts on behalf of a user (authorization code, refresh token, password, JWT bearer)

authentication.summary: User authorizes the app (or app uses password or JWT bearer grant) and it gets bearer tokens with the user's permissions limited to app scopes. The password grant precludes MFA; JWT bearer gets tokens without user authorization.

federation.details: JWT bearer grant: app signs an assertion whose sub names identityProviderId and username; trusted-client design, not workload federation.

ip_restriction.boundary: IP allowlist covers interactive sign-ins with Anypoint credentials only; SSO users excluded; token use by the app not documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token tied to user session (~60 min); refresh token 90 days

renewal.expiry_basis: refresh token 90 days; offline_access scope needed
renewal.summary: App exchanges refresh token for new access tokens while user is signed out.

administration.summary: Admins set Unrestricted (default) or Restricted authorization policy; Restricted enables an app allowlist. Internal apps are auto-approved unless that is disabled.
administration.conditions: Allowlist changes do not cut existing authorizations.

inventory.details: Access Management > Connected Apps > Authorizations lists authorized apps; GET /accounts/api/organizations/{organizationId}/connectedApplications lists apps.

network.ui: Access Management > Security Settings > IP Allowlist (add CIDR) > Enforce IP restrictions for login > Save. Covers sign-in with Anypoint credentials only, not SSO or token use

credentials.name: Anypoint Platform bearer token (user token from /accounts/login or SAML assertion)

authentication.summary: A user exchanges username/password at /accounts/login, or an IdP-initiated SAML response at the provider receive-id endpoint, for a bearer token with that user's permissions. Used by the CLI --bearer option.

federation.details: User token; SAML exchange requires IdP-initiated SSO.

ip_restriction.boundary: Applies to sign-ins with Anypoint credentials; not to SSO users. Not documented for API calls with an issued token.

renewal.summary: Log in again to get a new token.

administration.summary: Only controlled through org session timeout, MFA on direct sign-ins, and IP allowlist at login.
administration.conditions: MuleSoft says CLI use moves to connected apps.

sso.details: Federated users get the token through an IdP-initiated SAML assertion, but non-federated users keep using Anypoint credentials and /accounts/login.

offboard.details: Deleting a user in the IdP does not remove them from Anypoint; they must be deleted manually. Token validity follows the Default Session Timeout.

sso.ui: Access Management > Identity Providers > SAML 2.0 (configure IdP); MFA for SSO users is set in the IdP

credentials.name: Environment / business group client ID and client secret

authentication.summary: Each environment and the root business group has a client ID/secret used to pair customer-hosted Mule runtimes and API gateways; organization clients can get tokens via client_credentials. Root business group credentials grant permissions across all child business groups.

ip_restriction.boundary: The org IP allowlist covers only user sign-ins with Anypoint credentials; environment credentials are not covered. No other IP control documented.

renewal.summary: Secret is reused; reset via KB procedure or support.

administration.summary: Org admins can view the values; changing the secret points to a Salesforce Help article or support.

offboard.details: Credentials belong to an environment or business group, not a user.

inventory.details: Access Management > Environments shows each environment's client ID; Organization tab shows org/business group credentials.

credentials.name: API client application credentials (client ID / secret for API instances)

authentication.summary: Client applications registered in Exchange get a client ID and optional secret to call customer APIs protected by a client ID enforcement policy. These authenticate to customer APIs, not to Anypoint Platform APIs.

federation.details: Static credentials; external client providers (e.g. Entra ID, PingFederate) can be used instead.

ip_restriction.boundary: Only if the API owner applies the IP Allowlist policy to the API instance; applies to calls to that API, not platform-wide.

renewal.summary: Secret reusable; reset is an audited action.

administration.summary: API instance owner approves access requests (contracts) and can revoke, restore, or delete contracts in API Manager.
administration.conditions: Root org Organization Administrator for revoke/delete.

inventory.details: API Manager > API instance > Contracts lists contracts per instance; not all clients appear in the UI, and GET /accounts/api/organizations/{orgId}/clients is documented for the org-wide client count.

disable.ui: API Manager > (API instance) > SLA tiers: set tier to manual approval; then API Manager > API Administration > (instance) > Contracts > Approve / Reject
